frame: Inches, Pedro visualizer coordinates: x = 0 the red wall, y = 0 the audience wall.
notes: ONE SOURCE for BIOBUZZ obstacles. Read by tools/pedro-visualizer (src/config/defaults.ts, so the editor, path review and the MCP) and by Swerve Bring-Up's field fence (bundled into the APK through TeamCode/build.gradle's resources srcDir). Edit here, nowhere else.

The field IMAGE is Pedro Pathing's (Pedro-Pathing/Visualizer public/fields/biobuzz.webp at e976a746). Upstream ships no obstacles for it, so these are ours, measured off that image: 1080 px over 141.5 in is 0.13 in a pixel, which is the precision claimed.

Only what is in the way at drive height. The bottom of a HIVE is 25.5 in above the TILES (Manual V1 Fig 9-10) and an FTC ROBOT is at most 18 in tall, so a ROBOT drives under the CELLS, the crossbar at 43.95 in, and the Frame legs climbing to it. What is on the floor is the two base rails.

HIVE rails: Pedro's drawing puts them 2.42 in wide (outline included) over y 50.97-90.53, outer faces 50.32 in apart - the manual's 49.46 in frame width plus the outline, inside its +/- 1 in. Measured faces were averaged about the FIELD centre, since the real frame is symmetric and the pixel error is not.

FLOWERS are bolted to the perimeter wall and their lower ring sits on the TILES (Manual V1 Sec 9.7), so they are obstacles all the way down. Each is a chamfered hexagon on a wall bracket: 7.2 in across at the wall, 6.7 in at its widest, 4.6 in across the end, 5.1 in into the FIELD. Centres are on the TILE seam two seams round from a corner, to within 1.5 px of the drawing.
Every obstacle must stay CONVEX: the bring-up fence's distance and push-out geometry assumes it.
